2205.note: Turin Biblioteca Reale Varia 244 (Ottoboni/Villena papers 1704-06) has ciphered letters to a 'Mgr de la Tremoille Noirmoutier' with the decipherment scheme at c. 172 (a key in the volume); nothing online, no reading or edition found.

seen.where: Manus Online record for Torino, Biblioteca Reale, Manoscritti Varia, Varia.244 (CNMD 0000456583, inventory SM 14518), fetched 4 Nov 2026 through https://manus.iccu.sbn.it/o/manus-api/title?id=1871606 (permalink https://manus.iccu.sbn.it/cnmd/0000456583); no digital object or image link on the record; the lead has access 'archive'.
seen.extent: Cartaceo, 203 cc., 87 letters, drafts and notes, 1704-1706; the ciphered letters are at cc. 120, 125, 132 'e passim'; the record does not say how many leaves are in cipher.
seen.cipher: Manus (Storia del manoscritto): 'Alcune lettere (vd. cc. 120, 125 e passim, 132) indirizzate a un certo Monsignor de La Tremoille Noirmoutier, ed una risposta di questi, contengono codici cifrati; lo schema di decrittazione si trova alla c. 172.' The record describes the volume as the Ottoboni-Bottoni letters on the immunities dispute between the Papal court and the viceroy of Naples, marchese di Villena (Italian, some French, Spanish, Latin). It names no decipherment of the letters; the only decipherment material mentioned is the scheme on c. 172. Record created 14 Apr 2026 by R. Motisi; cited sources are Promis, Schede Ms. Varia and the library's Catalogo dei manoscritti Varia vol. IV, both unpublished.

seen.extent: Archivio di Stato di Palermo, Miscellanea archivistica, I serie, b. 68: 505 documents (formerly bb. 68-69) of Torrearsa's diplomatic correspondence as foreign minister, 14 Aug 1848 - 16 Feb 1849; by my count about 20 repertory entries mention a cipher, from one-page sheets to whole despatches.
seen.cipher: Repertory entries: no. 274, 24 Dec 1848, Gemelli 'Invia un modello per la corrispondenza in cifra, con allegato un dispaccio in cifra del Ministro'; no. 316, 27 Oct 1848, 'il foglio in cifra allegato con la sua versione'; no. 350, 11 Jan 1849, 'Allegato dispaccio in cifra con sua versione'; no. 441, 27 Jan 1849, Friddani and Amari, 'Dispaccio interamente in cifra con sua traduzione ... Contiene cinque allegati, tra cui la traduzione del dispaccio cifrato'. By my count 11 of the cipher entries (nos. 316, 321, 328, 332, 334, 350, 352, 399, 403, 431, 441) say a versione or traduzione is attached, so a contemporary decipherment is filed with those despatches; the other cipher entries (e.g. nos. 344, 412, 429) name none.

2218.note: Lang lists 12 of Teleki's Jan-Feb 1678 number-cipher letters as undeciphered, one of them (C.Tel.15 to Rhedey, 23 Jan 1678) was read by Hegedus in 2020 as a 37-value monoalphabetic code with nulls, so the other letters stay open; only that one letter's text was seen online (Gergely 1926 itself is not free).

seen.where: Hegedus Gyula, 'Teleki Mihaly titka. Egy 17. szazadi kodolt uzenet feltorese', NyelvVilag 23 (2020), pp. 60ff, PDF read 4 Nov 2026: https://publikaciotar.uni-bge.hu/1711/1/Hegedus_Nyelvvilag23.pdf ; it prints the number text of C.Tel.15 from Gergely Samuel (ed.), Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (MTT, Budapest 1926) p. 40, no. 38. The repertory of the 13 letters: Lang Benedek, Titkositas a kora ujkori Magyarorszagon (MTA thesis 2015), pp. 286-287, https://real-d.mtak.hu/922/7/dc_758_13_doktori_mu.pdf , read 4 Nov 2026. Gergely vol. VIII is not on Hungaricana (reviews only) or free elsewhere that I found; the lead has no access value.
seen.extent: Seen: one letter, C.Tel.15, 23 Jan 1678, about 240 numbers of 37 distinct values (1-79), clear first and last sentences. Not seen: the other letters of the lead (Gergely VIII nos. 9, 10, 20, 21, 25, 30, 36, 38, 41, 43, 50, 79, 87; short number-cipher letters, Lang IDs C.Tel.04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 21 etc.).
seen.cipher: Lang's repertory marks C.Tel.04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19 and 21 'magyar, szamok, valoszinuleg homof.' and 'megfejtetlen'; 10 and 18 'reszben feloldva, reszben megfejtetlen'. Hegedus (2020): 'A titkosírások megoldásával a kötetek kiadói sem boldogultak, vagy talán nem is próbálkoztak' (the volume editors did not solve the number sequences). The printed C.Tel.15 is number strings with the first and last sentences in clear and a short bracketed remark, no decipherment printed; his own solution is the article. Gap in what I saw: only C.Tel.15 was read as text; for the others I rely on Lang and Hegedus.

prior_art.decode: The letter-book copies are probably DECODE R4819-R4834 (Cluj, Eparhia Reformata, Pokoly-Nagy G2 506, 1650-1690; local list shows all 16 as status 4, Hungarian cleartext, no decipherment listed); not matched record by record and no images on the list. Teleki's own cipher keys are DECODE R647-R651, R665-R673 (NAH P1238 Teleki Mihaly Collection, cipher keys, 1660-1690, plus R648 for Ferenc Nadasdy 1671). No decipherment of the 1678 letters in the local list.

2236.note: Kuefstein's 27 Oct 1629 despatch to Ferdinand (ELTE Kezirattar G. 4 Fol. Tom. V p. 1461) is a full page of graphic-sign cipher, seen in the facsimile plate of Donath 1964 with no decipherment on it; Lang marks it megfejtetlen, and sibling drafts in the volume have plaintext over the signs.

seen.where: Donath Regina, 'A diplomaciai titkosiras XVII. szazadi hasznalatahoz', Magyar Konyvszemle 80 (1964) no. 1, pp. 55-62, plate on p. 57 (whole-issue PDF https://epa.oszk.hu/00000/00021/00254/pdf/MKSZ_EPA00021_1964_80_01_00254.pdf , PDF page 63, viewed 4 Nov 2026; article PDF .../MKSZ_EPA00021_1964_80_01_047-073.pdf). The plate is captioned with the folio number 1461 in the corner. The ELTE manuscript itself (Egyetemi Konyvtar, Kezirattar, G. 4 Fol. Tom. V.) was not found digitised.
seen.extent: One despatch on one page (Tom. V p. 1461), about 22 lines of cipher signs, the salutation and the dating line 'Octobris ... 629' in clear; Lang counts it 'majdnem teljes' (nearly complete) cipher.
seen.cipher: Facsimile: the whole body is graphic signs (no word division), with a German address formula at the top, the dating line and the signature in clear; nothing is written between the lines or in the margin. Lang 2015 p. 259 (C.Kuf.16): 'gyenge homof., latin abc, zömében graf. jelek, csak a mgh-knak kettő jel, a többinek egy'; key T.Kuf.01 and the despatch both 'megfejtetlen'. Donath's note 2 lists the cipher material of the volume: Tom. V 469-472, 495-496, 535, 559-560, 615-616, 685, 747-748, 755-762, 821-826, 829-836, 855-858, 957-958, 1069-1073, 1461; her deciphered specimens are other letters (Tom. V pp. 615, 755, 1069).

1602.note: BNE RES/227/120-121 and 127-129 viewed: the Duke of Feria's 1622 letters to Coloma carry cipher passages (digits and signs) with plaintext written beside them in the left margin, so the cipher is partly read by an adjacent decipherment, not open.

seen.extent: RES/227/120 (Milan, 26 Oct 1622): 2 pages, about 5 lines of cipher at the foot of image 5 and about 14 lines on image 6. RES/227/121 (Milan, 23 Nov 1622, on the death of Baltasar de Zuniga): clear text only, no cipher. RES/227/127-129 (3 and 10 Aug, 14 Sept 1622, 'cifradas en parte' per BNE): image 5 shows about 5 lines of cipher with margin plaintext; 128-129 not opened. Spanish.
seen.cipher: BNE note: 'Son dos cartas con firmas autografas y sello de placa. La primera carta, cifrada en parte. Fechadas en Milan, 26 octubre y 23 noviembre 1622'. On RES/227/120 images 5-6 the cipher is runs of digits, letter-like forms and other signs, and in the left margin beside the runs is written plaintext, e.g. (my approximate reading) 'con la paz que el Rey de Francia ha concluydo con los hereges, que desembaraçado de las cosas domesticas de su casa ...' (image 5) and 'el Duque de Mantua y Veneciano' (image 6). On RES/227/127 image 5 the margin beside the cipher reads 'Muy gran vuelta que ha hecho Saboya ... han hecho franceses ... Conde de Mansfelt ha entrado en Flandes'. The margin text appears to be in the same ink and hand as the letter, so a decipherment is written with the cipher; the remainder of each cipher passage was not compared line by line.

prior_art.decode: Not on DECODE: local list has no HHStA England Varia record; DECODE's Lisola items are the 1672 Geheime Staatsregistratur set (R1914-R1918, R2040), a different series and year; known.py on '6428100', 'England Varia', Buckingham, Molina finds only this lead, its sweep file and the catalogue entry for the neighbouring England Varia 5-4-17 (entry 1745) and entry 513 (Spanien Varia group with Lisola's 1667 letter on the Swedish alliance).
prior_art.tomokiyo: cryptiana.web.fc2.com: fetched the pages linked from code/crypto.htm (about 290, including GL.htm, unsolved.htm, habsburg.htm, gualterio.htm, spanish*.htm) on 4 Nov 2026 and grepped them for Lisola, Buckingham, Arlington, Molina: Lisola only in variable3.htm (a key of about 1657-59 with Cromwell, Lisola, Penaranda); Buckingham and Arlington only in English-cipher pages (Charles II, Morland, Wallis); nothing on this conference.
prior_art.lasry: Web searches 4 Nov 2026 (Lasry/HistoCrypt on Lisola or 1667 conferences; Lisola conference 24 December 1667) found no item; GL.htm has none.
prior_art.edition: No edition found: web searches for a Dec 1667 Buckingham-Arlington-Molina-Lisola conference found only general Triple Alliance and Lisola literature (Pribram's Lisola biography of 1894 and his Leopold I-Poetting edition are cited by the Historical Journal article but were not opened, so a printed text cannot be ruled out).
prior_art.literature: Web searches returned the Historical Journal article on Lisola and English opposition to Louis XIV and State Papers calendars; none mentions this protocol or a decipherment.

vetting.key_check: No key filed with this item (AIS: no related units); none held here or on DECODE for Lisola in London 1667. The c.1657-59 Lisola key on Tomokiyo's variable3.htm is a different system and was not tried. Nothing tested.
